title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: The user-opt-in default is documented for Scheduled triggers, but not for the broader direct-trigger capability this briefing explicitly distinguishes from it. The instruction to identify schedule owners in Overview also lacks support: that page documents a creator column, not a current-owner column.

claims.claim: The planned capability belongs to Power Automate.
claims.quote: "title": "Power Automate: Direct triggers for desktop flows"; "products": ["Power Automate"]

claims.claim: A cloud flow can start a desktop flow with Run a flow built with Power Automate for desktop.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The cloud-flow route requires a desktop flow connection.
claims.quote: A configured desktop flow connection.

claims.claim: The cloud-trigger page lists an appropriate licence for attended runs.
claims.quote: To run the triggered desktop flows, you need to have the appropriate license (for attended runs) or an unattended add-on (for unattended runs).

claims.claim: The cloud-trigger page lists an unattended add-on for unattended runs.
claims.quote: To run the triggered desktop flows, you need to have the appropriate license (for attended runs) or an unattended add-on (for unattended runs).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cloud-trigger page identifies the connection creator as the user needing the appropriate licence.
claims.quote: The user who needs to have the appropriate license is the creator of the connection.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified which cloud-route checks carry over to broader event-trigger cases.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Opened schedule-desktop-flows, trigger-desktop-flows and desktop-flow-connections; the scheduling prerequisites are stated, not broader event cases.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: A user creates a scheduled trigger and turns on Enable to activate it.
claims.quote: To activate the trigger immediately after you create it, turn on Enable.

claims.claim: Leaving Enable off saves a scheduled trigger disabled.
claims.quote: Leave it off to save the trigger as disabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap's direct-trigger capability has a user-opt-in default.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows enabled default existing flows automatic admin switch. Read roadmap record and schedule-desktop-flows. Only Scheduled triggers has documented maker activation; no source identifies it as the entire roadmap capability.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Keep the documented Enable behaviour explicitly scoped to Scheduled triggers (preview), and retain the sentence that Microsoft has not stated arrival behaviour for the broader event-trigger capability.

claims.claim: Arrival behaviour and changes to existing flows are not stated for the broader event-trigger capability.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows enabled default existing flows automatic admin switch. Read roadmap record and schedule-desktop-flows; neither describes changes to existing flows for broader event triggers.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern desktop flow modules.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.
claims.fix: Narrow the risk rationale's 'whether data policies cover the new route is unconfirmed' to 'whether desktop flow connector policies govern the new triggering route is unconfirmed', matching the body and row note rather than casting doubt on the documented module policies.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: The application of desktop flow connector policies to the new triggering route is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduled triggers desktop DLP connector policy; direct triggers desktop flows DLP data policies. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and prevent-data-loss. The connector is governable, but the new route is not identified as invoking that connector.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers select an execution connection reference for a machine or machine group.
claims.quote: Connection reference: Select an existing connection reference, or select New connection reference to create one. Machine or machine group: Select the machine or machine group that runs the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Connection-reference creation selects an authentication method.
claims.quote: Under Connect, select the authentication method.

claims.claim: Connection-reference creation supplies credentials or uses a Windows credential.
claims.quote: Enter the required credentials, or turn on Windows credential to use a Windows credential.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Identity and machine-session details for broader event-trigger cases remain unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and desktop-flow-connections; read run-unattended-desktop-flows search excerpt. No broader event-specific identity mechanism was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The schedule owner can manage schedules.
claims.quote: users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage desktop-flow schedules, in addition to the schedule owner.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users assigned Power Automate Operator can manage schedules where Scheduled triggers is available.
claims.quote: In environments where Scheduled triggers is available, users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage desktop-flow schedules, in addition to the schedule owner.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Operator includes permissions for the Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance tables.
claims.quote: The Operator role includes organization-level permissions for the Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Those Operator permissions apply across the assigned environment.
claims.quote: These permissions apply to the entire environment where the role is assigned, not just to records owned by the operator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Operator itself does not grant permission to edit the desktop flow definition.
claims.quote: The Operator role itself doesn't grant permission to create or modify the underlying desktop flow definition. Other security roles assigned to the user might grant those permissions.

claims.claim: Learn advises securing a machine before cloud-triggered desktop runs.
claims.quote: Before using a machine to run desktop flows from the cloud, ensure that the machine is secured and the machine's admins are trusted.

claims.claim: Learn advises trusting the machine's admins before cloud-triggered desktop runs.
claims.quote: Before using a machine to run desktop flows from the cloud, ensure that the machine is secured and the machine's admins are trusted.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an approval step for the new direct-trigger route.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduled triggers desktop frequency limit approval; direct triggers desktop flows approval. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and run-desktop-flows-url-shortcuts; URL confirmation is a different route, not a scheduled-trigger approval step.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a direct-trigger frequency limit.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduled triggers desktop frequency maximum minimum limit approval. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and Logic Apps recurrence scheduling. Read cloud-flow limits excerpt; no direct-trigger-specific frequency limit is stated.

claims.claim: The cloud-trigger page documents up to 70 desktop flow runs per minute per connection.
claims.quote: We currently support up to 70 desktop flows runs per minute for every connection.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether that connection run-rate limit applies to direct triggers.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows default limits; Scheduled triggers desktop frequency maximum minimum limit. Opened trigger-desktop-flows and schedule-desktop-flows; no statement extends the cloud-route 70-runs limit to direct triggers.

claims.where: controls[0]; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant-wide availability switch for direct triggers is documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers tenant environment disable admin switch API Flow trigger table; Scheduled triggers admin PowerShell pac availability switch. Read scheduling page, Flow Trigger table and pac admin excerpts; only per-record or general controls appeared.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Scheduled triggers can be disabled through Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > Overview > scheduled trigger > More commands > Disable.
claims.quote: select the environment where you want to manage scheduled triggers. In the left navigation pane, select Automation center. Under Manage, select Scheduled triggers (Preview). On the Overview tab, open the More commands menu
claims.fix: Include environment selection: Power Automate > environment > Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > Overview > scheduled trigger > More commands > Disable, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs.
claims.quote: Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.

claims.claim: Disabling retains the scheduled trigger's configuration.
claims.quote: Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require the licensing and capacity for the selected attended or unattended run mode.
claims.quote: The licensing and capacity required for the selected attended or unattended run mode.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium includes attended desktop automation.
claims.quote: this license includes the ability for users to register their workstation, to create unlimited desktop flows, and to execute their desktop flows in attended mode on their registered machine through an attended bot borne by the license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing overview directs unattended desktop flows generally to Process licences or pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No direct-trigger-specific licensing change is published.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop price meter licensing; direct triggers desktop flows pay-as-you-go rate exemption exception licensing change. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and licensing/types; run-mode requirements are stated, not a distinct direct-trigger entitlement.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's 'Direct-trigger licensing is not yet published.' with 'No direct-trigger-specific licensing change is published.' This preserves the distinction from the documented run-mode licensing in the body.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing describes the documented user-licence, capacity and consumption options.
claims.quote: Power Automate supports both user and capacity licensing. For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The Power Automate flow-run meter is in preview and covers desktop flows in pay-as-you-go environments.
claims.quote: Power Automate flow runs (preview): Flow runs for premium cloud flows and desktop flows.

claims.claim: Attended desktop-run charges depend on the user's licence entitlements.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are charged per run.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.claim: No direct-trigger-specific rate is published.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows pay-as-you-go rate exemption exception licensing change. Opened pay-as-you-go-meters, licensing/types and schedule-desktop-flows; general desktop-run rates and exemptions are stated, not a separate direct-trigger rule.

claims.claim: Variable cost is consistent with the documented flow-run meter.
claims.quote: The Power Automate meters enable users to build and/or run premium Power Automate flows and to pay for their usage based on the number of times these flows run instead of purchasing standalone Power Automate licenses.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a work or school account with target-environment access.
claims.quote: A work or school account that can access the target Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a published desktop flow the user owns or co-owns.
claims.quote: A published desktop flow that you own or co-own.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a machine or machine group registered in the same environment.
claims.quote: A machine or machine group registered in the same environment.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a connection reference.
claims.quote: A connection reference for the target machine or machine group. You can create the connection reference while creating the scheduled trigger.

claims.claim: The broader event-trigger capability has no published event-specific user scope.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Read roadmap and schedule-desktop-flows; broad roadmap scope and scheduling prerequisites exist, not an event-specific operational specification.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the Scheduled triggers preview is not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: The Overview tab under Scheduled triggers (Preview) in Automation center lists schedules.
claims.quote: The Overview tab lists the scheduled triggers available to you. Created by: The user who created the scheduled trigger. Displayed by default: No.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the data-policy list.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.
claims.fix: For configuring an existing policy, extend the path to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > Assign connectors'; the cited page documents selection and connector classification beyond the list.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a DLP policy from the supplied policy definition in Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy. Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.claim: The checklist's Scheduled triggers review control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review which desktop flows have a scheduled trigger and who owns them, using the Overview tab'. Table rows: tenant-wide availability switch; desktop flow modules and connectors data policy.
claims.fix: The After rollout step directing readers to review schedules in Overview has no corresponding control row. Remove that navigation-specific checklist step; a correction need not add a row.

claims.claim: A data policy can manage both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed like other connectors.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Adding desktop flow modules to data policies causes noncompliant desktop flows to be evaluated and suspended.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: The tenant-level data-policy instructions require Power Platform Administrator.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies require Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse qualification.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies in environments with a Dataverse database require System Administrator instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Readers can identify the current owner of scheduled triggers using the Overview tab.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Scheduled triggers Overview owner Created by schedule owner columns. Opened schedule-desktop-flows; Overview documents Created by, not Owner. Read Flow Trigger reference excerpts distinguishing writable ownerid from record creation.
claims.fix: Remove 'and who owns them' from the Overview-based checklist instruction. The scheduling page documents a Created by column, not a current-owner column; do not describe the creator as necessarily the current owner.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not identify Scheduled triggers as the capability it describes.
claims.quote: Desktop flows will support direct triggers, enabling automations to start in response to supported events without requiring an intermediary cloud flow.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say whether flows can return data through the event-trigger route.
claims.quote: Desktop flows will support direct triggers, enabling automations to start in response to supported events without requiring an intermediary cloud flow.

claims.claim: No direct-trigger-specific exception to the general desktop-run meter is published.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows pay-as-you-go rate exemption exception licensing change. Opened pay-as-you-go-meters, licensing/types and schedule-desktop-flows; the exemptions stated are general run-mode and licence rules.

claims.claim: No roles specific to the broader event-trigger capability are published.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Opened schedule-desktop-flows; owner and Operator schedule permissions are documented, not separate broader-event permissions.

claims.claim: No prerequisites specific to broader event-trigger cases are published.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Opened schedule-desktop-flows and trigger-desktop-flows; the stated prerequisites concern scheduling and cloud-triggered runs.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for broader event-trigger cases are not published beyond the roadmap targets.
claims.quote: Searched: direct triggers desktop flows events identity account machine session prerequisites roles rollout. Read roadmap record and schedule-desktop-flows; gradual regional rollout is stated for the scheduling preview, not a broader event-trigger rollout.
